description: Authoritative machine-readable knowledge base for IPsec VPN security, compliance baselines, and RFC/NIST standards mapping.

rules.title: Insecure or Deprecated Cipher Algorithm
rules.description: The VPN configuration utilizes a legacy, weak, or deprecated cipher algorithm (e.g., DES, 3DES, Blowfish, RC4, or NULL encryption). These algorithms do not provide adequate confidentiality against modern cryptanalytic attacks.
rules.recommendation: Immediately migrate to a modern Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) cipher suite, such as AES-256-GCM or AES-128-GCM.

references.title: IPsec Cryptographic Algorithms
references.guidance: Single DES and Triple DES (3DES) are disallowed for Federal applications. Modern deployments must adopt AES-GCM (RFC 4106) with 128-bit or 256-bit keys.

references.title: ESP Encryption Algorithms
references.guidance: DES is MUST NOT; Triple-DES (3DES) is NOT RECOMMENDED; NULL encryption is NOT RECOMMENDED without authentication.

rules.title: Legacy Non-AEAD Cipher Mode (CBC)
rules.description: The VPN tunnel uses Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode (e.g., AES-CBC) rather than Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD). CBC mode requires separate integrity checks and is historically susceptible to padding oracle attacks.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade tunnel transform proposals to authenticated encryption (AES-256-GCM or AES-128-GCM) where supported by peers.

references.title: AEAD Cipher Suites
references.guidance: NIST strongly recommends AEAD algorithms (AES-GCM) over combined encryption-plus-authentication suites (AES-CBC + HMAC).

references.title: ESP Encryption Algorithms
references.guidance: AES-128-GCM and AES-256-GCM are MUST; AES-128-CBC is MAY for backward compatibility only.

rules.title: Modern Authenticated Encryption (AEAD)
rules.description: The VPN tunnel employs a modern Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data suite (AES-256-GCM or AES-128-GCM), providing both strong payload confidentiality and authenticated ciphertext integrity in a single cryptographic primitive.
rules.recommendation: Maintain the current AEAD transform proposal.

references.title: Recommended IPsec Ciphers
references.guidance: AES-256-GCM (RFC 4106) provides optimal confidentiality and performance with 256 bits of cryptographic strength.

references.title: ESP Encryption Algorithms
references.guidance: AES-128-GCM and AES-256-GCM are standard MUST implement suites.

rules.title: Insecure / Broken Diffie-Hellman Group
rules.description: The key exchange uses an obsolete Diffie-Hellman group with modulus under 1536 bits (e.g., Group 1: 768-bit MODP or Group 2: 1024-bit MODP). These groups are vulnerable to precomputation attacks (Logjam).
rules.recommendation: Immediately transition to Group 19 (256-bit random ECP / NIST P-256), Group 20 (384-bit random ECP), or Group 14 (2048-bit MODP).

references.title: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange Groups
references.guidance: Diffie-Hellman groups providing less than 112 bits of security (MODP < 2048 bits) are strictly disallowed.

references.title: Diffie-Hellman Groups for IKEv2
references.guidance: Group 1 (768-bit MODP) and Group 2 (1024-bit MODP) are MUST NOT.

rules.title: Legacy Diffie-Hellman Group (Sub-2048 bit)
rules.description: The DH group used (e.g. Group 5: 1536-bit MODP) is deprecated by modern standards as having an inadequate security margin against well-resourced state-level adversaries.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade to Diffie-Hellman Group 19 (ecp256), Group 20 (ecp384), or Group 14 (modp2048).

references.title: Diffie-Hellman Groups
references.guidance: MODP groups with modulus size under 2048 bits are deprecated and disallowed for Federal use.

references.title: Diffie-Hellman Groups for IKEv2
references.guidance: Group 5 (1536-bit MODP) is SHOULD NOT.

rules.title: Strong / Recommended Diffie-Hellman Group
rules.description: The key exchange utilizes a strong modern Diffie-Hellman group: Elliptic Curve Group 19 (NIST P-256), Group 20 (NIST P-384), or 2048-bit MODP (Group 14).
rules.recommendation: Maintain the current Diffie-Hellman group configuration.

references.title: Diffie-Hellman Groups
references.guidance: Group 19 (ecp256) and Group 20 (ecp384) provide superior cryptographic security margin and computational efficiency.

references.title: Diffie-Hellman Groups for IKEv2
references.guidance: Group 19 (256-bit Random ECP) is RECOMMENDED; Group 14 (2048-bit MODP) is MUST.

rules.title: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) Disabled
rules.description: Perfect Forward Secrecy is disabled for Child SAs. New Child SA keys are derived from the existing IKE SA keying material without an independent Diffie-Hellman exchange. If the IKE SA master key is ever compromised, all past session traffic can be retroactively decrypted.
rules.recommendation: Enable Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) in Child SA configurations.

references.title: IKE Security Features
references.guidance: PFS ensures that compromise of a single key permits access only to data protected by that specific key. NIST recommends enabling PFS for Child SAs.

references.title: The CREATE_CHILD_SA Exchange
references.guidance: A new Diffie-Hellman exchange in CREATE_CHILD_SA provides Perfect Forward Secrecy, ensuring that key compromises do not cascade to past sessions.

rules.title: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) Enabled
rules.description: Perfect Forward Secrecy is active. Each renegotiation of Child SAs executes an independent Diffie-Hellman exchange, ensuring cryptographic key isolation across all sessions.
rules.recommendation: Maintain PFS enabled across all tunnel configurations.

references.title: Forward Secrecy Best Practice
references.guidance: PFS is a vital defense-in-depth measure against retroactive traffic decryption.

rules.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Detected
rules.description: The VPN tunnel negotiates using IKEv1 (RFC 2409). IKEv1 is deprecated due to structural protocol vulnerabilities, lack of native EAP/MOBIKE support, susceptibility to offline dictionary attacks in Aggressive Mode, and amplification DDoS vectors.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade gateway endpoints to IKEv2 (RFC 7296). Disable IKEv1 listener daemons.

references.title: IKE Protocol Versions
references.guidance: Organizations must transition all IPsec VPNs to IKEv2. IKEv1 is legacy and should not be used in new deployments.

references.title: Differences between IKEv1 and IKEv2
references.guidance: IKEv2 replaces IKEv1, streamlining negotiations from 4-6 messages down to 4, eliminating Aggressive Mode flaws, and integrating anti-DoS mechanisms.

rules.title: Modern IKEv2 Protocol Active
rules.description: The VPN session utilizes IKEv2 (RFC 7296), featuring robust cookie-based anti-DoS handshakes, streamlined message exchanges, and native rekeying.
rules.recommendation: Maintain IKEv2 as the sole active key exchange protocol.

references.title: IKEv2 Overview
references.guidance: IKEv2 is the standard protocol for performing mutual authentication and establishing Security Associations for IPsec.

rules.title: Deprecated Integrity Algorithm (MD5 / SHA-1)
rules.description: The integrity or authentication suite utilizes MD5 or SHA-1 (e.g., HMAC-MD5, HMAC-SHA1). These hash algorithms suffer from practical collision attacks.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade authentication algorithm to HMAC-SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-384, or use AEAD ciphers with built-in 128-bit authentication tags (AES-GCM).

references.title: Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms
references.guidance: SHA-1 and MD5 are disallowed for digital signature and integrity generation across all security protocols.

references.title: Integrity Algorithms for IKEv2
references.guidance: AUTH_HMAC_MD5_96 is MUST NOT; AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 is SHOULD NOT; AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128 is MUST.

rules.title: Zero SPI Detected in ESP Header
rules.description: An ESP packet has an SPI value of 0x00000000. Under RFC 4303, the SPI value 0 is strictly reserved and MUST NOT be used for an operational Security Association.
rules.recommendation: Inspect gateway implementation for memory corruption, uninitialized buffer states, or malformed packet injection.

references.title: Security Parameters Index (SPI)
references.guidance: The set of SPI values in the range 1 through 255 are reserved by IANA. The value 0 is reserved for local implementation use and MUST NOT be sent on the wire.

rules.title: ESP Sequence Number Anomaly / Potential Replay
rules.description: Observable ESP sequence numbers demonstrate non-monotonic regression or significant duplicate packet indices, indicating network reordering, packet duplication, or potential replay attack attempts.
rules.recommendation: Verify anti-replay window configuration on the receiving gateway and investigate underlying transit network path.

references.title: Replay Protection
references.guidance: ESP implementations MUST support the anti-replay service. The receiver uses a sliding window to detect and reject replayed packets.

rules.title: Site-to-Site Tunnel Mode Active
rules.description: The VPN operates in Tunnel mode, encapsulating the entire original IP datagram within a new outer IP header. This provides optimal security architecture for gateway-to-gateway topology.
rules.recommendation: Maintain Tunnel mode for multi-host and gateway-to-gateway environments.

references.title: Tunnel Mode versus Transport Mode
references.guidance: Tunnel mode encapsulates the inner IP datagram completely, hiding inner subnet topology and host addresses from transit networks.
